replacement.note: NOT an upgrade chain. Each of these seven grants exactly ONE distinct Strike, one per effect class (slow / snare / interrupt / mana drain / root / spell slow / dispel), so a higher-level member is a different tool, not a stronger version of the one below it. They 'replace' one another only in the mechanical sense that ALL utility poisons share ONE coat slot (see stacking). Real upgrade relations exist but they cross into the combination tier: each single-Strike poison is strictly subsumed by every combination poison that grants its Strike (e.g. Banishing Poison 20 is subsumed by Antimagic 36 and Mage Bane 39). That relation is a lattice, not a chain, and is recorded per-member in the combination line below.

conflicts.detail: ONE utility poison at a time, full stop - the two utility lines here are one exclusivity group, split only by tier for readability. Wiki Rogue page, Poisons section: 'Only one utility poison can be active at a time, but all other combat poisons can be active simultaneously, unless otherwise noted on their respective descriptions.' Every utility poison's own description repeats 'This is considered a utility Poison, only one of which may be active at a time.' The game states this in the log too: 'Your Antimagic Poison spell did not take hold. (Blocked by Neurotoxic Poison.)' - a failed coat with no coat line following.
conflicts.source: scripts/sources/cache/classes/Rogue.wikitext (Poisons section + every utility row's description); log evidence quoted in src/shared/poisons.ts

stacksWith.detail: The utility slot is independent of the three combat venom slots. One utility + one member of each combat line = 4 concurrent coats, at any level. Independently corroborated off-wiki: everquestguides.com Beta Watch (Apr 27 - May 2, 2026) lists 'Rogue 1 utility + 3 combat poisons simultaneously'.

stacking.notes: Coats are character-global, not per-weapon: 'Poisons apply globally to all melee and but not ranged attacks, not on a per-weapon basis.' Duration is Permanent - 'Once applied poisons last until class swap or character death.' Coating takes 2.5s; reuse timer 5 sec. Strikes are checked against the target's Poison Resistance and are not reflectable. When a utility coat is swapped the log prints 'The poison dries from the blade.' in the same second as the new coat.

replacement.note: NOT an upgrade chain either. All eight grant exactly two Strikes and no two members grant the same PAIR - the eight pairs are drawn from the seven base Strikes with no repeats, so a level-42 Paralytic is not 'better than' a level-39 Mage Bane, it is a different pair (melee+spell slow vs mana drain+dispel). What IS strict is the cross-tier relation: every combination poison strictly subsumes the two single-Strike poisons whose Strikes it grants, and it always sits at a higher level than both. Since the whole utility roster shares one slot, coating any member clears whatever was on the blades - 'replacement' in the slot sense is universal and says nothing about power.

conflicts.detail: Same single slot - see that line's conflict entry. Splitting the utility roster into two lines here is presentational (base effect vs combined effect); mechanically all 15 utility poisons are ONE exclusivity group and at most one is ever coated.

MEDIUM CONFIDENCE, no Legends text found. Weakening Strike is an attack-speed debuff on the mob (DB: 'Decrease Melee Haste by 15%'). Prior shaman-wave research recorded that attack-speed debuffs occupy one slot on the mob and a shaman slow and an enchanter slow overwrite each other, strongest wins. If that slot model holds, the rogue's Weakening Strike (from Binding 25, Neurotoxic 28, Paralytic 42, and Weakening Poison 4) would not stack with a shaman/enchanter slow and would be the weaker of the two. NOTHING on the Legends Rogue page states this - flagged, not asserted.
conflicts.source: docs/research/spell-lines/lines-merged.json (shaman `slow` line stacking note); no Legends-authored confirmation

stacksWith.detail: Independent slots. A combination utility coat sits alongside up to three combat venoms.

stacking.notes: The two Strikes a combination poison grants are separate proc rolls against the same melee swing stream; each rolls against the target's Poison Resistance independently. IMPORTANT for attribution (this is why the overlay cannot name a coat from an emote): FOUR poisons grant Weakening Strike (Weakening, Binding, Neurotoxic, Paralytic) and its emote "<mob>'s limbs move slower!" names no caster, so a slow landing proves 'a rogue slow proc', never a specific coat. Same shape for Befuddling Strike (5 sources), Clumsiness Strike (4), Concussive (3), Banishing (3), Hobbling (3), Grounding (2).

openQuestions: NAME CONFLICT at level 30: spells.json has 'Mind Wrack Poison', the wiki Rogue roster has 'Mind Break Poison'. Identical description (Concussive Strike + Clumsiness Strike). One source is stale. Until resolved the overlay should match both spellings.

Weakening Strike magnitude disagrees between sources: the wiki table's Max Effect cell says '-35% Attack Speed' with duration 2:42, while its own description text says 0:03:30 and the spells.json row says 'Decrease Melee Haste by 15%' / 3 Min 30 Sec. The DB row is what the client reports, so 15% is the safer number, but the disagreement is unexplained. Same shape for Clumsiness Strike (wiki duration cell 2:18 vs description 0:03:30).

Does the rogue's Weakening Strike share the mob's attack-speed-debuff slot with a shaman or enchanter slow? Prior shaman-wave research says attack-speed debuffs occupy one slot and the strongest wins, which would mean a rogue slow is overwritten by (and cannot stack with) any real shaman slow. NO Legends-authored text confirms this for poison Strikes. Unresolved.

Do the rogue's poison-school DoTs (Blood Siphon / Blood Draw Strike) share a DoT slot with shaman or necromancer poison DoTs (Envenomed Breath / Envenomed Bolt / Venom of the Snake)? No evidence either way. Note that every Strike carries 'Increase Poison Counter by N' (9 on the two checked), so they ARE the same counter system a Cure Poison strips - which suggests a shared mechanic but says nothing about slot sharing.
Do Hobbling Strike (snare) and Grounding Strike (root) contend with ranger/druid snare and root lines on the mob? Untested and unstated.

The Rogue page itself asks, unanswered: 'does that include melee special attacks like slam? spellblade? backstab?' - i.e. whether Backstab and other melee specials roll the poison proc. Leave the overlay agnostic until answered.

Why do exactly these 9 poisons carry a `classes: '* Rogue - Level N'` tag in spells.json while the other 11 do not? All 20 exist as rows. The 9 tagged rows also share two other oddities: durationText 'Permanent' (the 11 untagged rows say 'Instant', which contradicts the wiki's Permanent for every poison) and a BLANK name in their first 'Add Melee Proc:' effect. That is a scrape/template artifact on the wiki side, not a gameplay difference - but it means any class-list-driven UI shows 9 of 20 rogue poisons unless it also reads the untagged rows.
